tool_args.rationale: The five paid observations end at H=0.48, more than 40 times shorter than the forecast horizon. The slow-horizon probe directly tests whether adaptation eventually offsets or reverses the fast positive response and constrains that effect where the forecast is scored.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the five-parameter sink-coupled dual-horizon model now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Over the short pilot window, the slow term primarily constrains the ratio of adaptation amplitude to time constant. Fits that agree there can disagree at H=20.3.
It costs only 0.5 less, and there is no indication that it samples the long horizons needed to separate slow amplitude from time constant.
Positive short-window responses do not rule out a delayed reversal.
